Granuloma with central debris

A patient has weight loss, chronic cough, and an upper-lobe cavitary lesion. Biopsy shows epithelioid macrophages surrounding a central granular acellular area; acid-fast organisms are identified. Which necrosis pattern is most consistent with these findings?

  1. Caseous necrosis
  2. Coagulative necrosis
  3. Enzymatic fat necrosis
  4. Fibrinoid necrosis
  5. Isolated apoptotic-body formation
Answer and explanation

Caseous necrosis

Tuberculous granulomas commonly contain central caseous material.

Option explanations

Caseous necrosis: Tuberculous granulomas commonly contain central caseous material.

Coagulative necrosis: Recognizable tissue outlines are not the defining feature of caseation.

Enzymatic fat necrosis: This centers on adipose tissue and calcium soaps.

Fibrinoid necrosis: This is a vessel-wall pattern rather than the granuloma center.

Isolated apoptotic-body formation: Apoptosis involves individual-cell fragments rather than a large caseous center.
